name: Kit
tagline: Email marketing and automation platform for creators

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked; 2026 public sources list Creator from $39/month at up to 1,000 subscribers, with price scaling by subscriber count.

tiers.name: Newsletter
tiers.limits: Up to 1,000 email subscribers on pricing card, unlimited landing pages/forms/email broadcasts, 1 basic Visual Automation, tags/segments, sell products/subscriptions.
tiers.notes: Comparison copy on page also referenced a higher free-subscriber ceiling, so the pricing-card number is used here.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.limits: 1,000 subscribers at starting tier, Visual Automations, creator commerce, automations and integrations.
tiers.notes: $390/year annual price; prices scale by subscriber count.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1,000 subscribers at starting tier, unlimited users, engagement analytics, subscriber signals.
tiers.notes: $790/year annual price; prices scale by subscriber count.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; up to 1,000 email subscribers on pricing card, 1 basic Visual Automation, unlimited landing pages/forms/broadcasts.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual saves about 17%/2 months free
pricing.hiddenCosts: Prices scale by subscriber count; paid newsletter/product payments may have separate commerce/payment processing costs.

verdictSummary: A simple newsletter sender is buildable, but Kit's value is deliverability, subscriber forms, automations, recommendations, commerce, migrations, and creator-specific flows.
coreLoopDIY: Build subscriber forms, a campaign editor, segmentation, simple automations, and send via an email API.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because email marketing is part deliverability and part business workflow.

priorArt.name: Listmonk
priorArt.desc: Open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager suitable for self-hosted campaigns.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms and basic automation without creator-specific furniture; the daily send cap is the catch.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, consent records, and message events live in Brevo's cloud; contacts can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo Free handles campaigns, forms, and basic automation, but it lacks Kit's creator commerce, recommendation network, and audience-monetization workflow while imposing a daily send cap.
facts.setupBlocker: Authenticating a custom sending domain requires adding DNS records.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: A straightforward creator list with forms and a welcome sequence; monetization is not pretending to be included.

facts.dataFormat: Lists, campaigns, automations, and reporting data live in EmailOctopus' cloud; contacts and reports can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: EmailOctopus Free is a straightforward newsletter service, but it lacks Kit's creator commerce, recommendation swaps, and creator-specific subscriber funnels.
facts.setupBlocker: You must verify a sender address or domain; DNS authentication is the first technical step.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.desc: The vendor's free plan covers 10,000 subscribers, unlimited sends, one sequence and one automation.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, tags, forms, broadcasts, sequences, purchases, and analytics live in Kit's cloud; subscriber and chart data export as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kit Free preserves the same platform, but only one basic visual automation and one sequence are included and one recommendation slot is controlled by Kit.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no software install, but custom-domain sending requires DNS authentication and the free plan keeps one Kit-managed recommendation slot.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Generous hosted campaigns, forms and workflows; creator commerce and recommendation swaps are missing.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, automations, and engagement events live in Sender's cloud; subscriber data can be exported.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender Free offers capable campaigns, forms, and workflows, but it does not replace Kit's creator products, paid-newsletter tooling, or recommendation network.
facts.setupBlocker: A custom sending domain must be verified with DNS records for reliable delivery.

notes: Good creator-economy entry; not a no, but the moat is operational.
prompt:
Build me a personal newsletter tool to replace Kit for a small list. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS. Subscribers, campaigns, sends, and
  events all in one SQLite file.
- A public /subscribe form with double opt-in: signed confirmation link by email
  before anyone is added. One-click unsubscribe link in every footer, no login.
- Compose campaigns in Markdown in the admin UI (bound to localhost or my VPN
  only), preview rendered HTML, send to everyone or to a tag.
- Sends go through Amazon SES or Postmark (key in .env) at a throttled rate, with
  per-recipient status recorded; bounce and complaint webhooks auto-suppress bad
  addresses.
- Tags on subscribers, plus one simple welcome autoresponder: a single email sent N
  minutes after confirmation.
- CSV import and export of the list, so I can arrive from Kit and leave anytime.
- No accounts beyond mine, no telemetry, no tracking pixels by default.
- Out of scope: landing pages, visual automation builders, the creator
  recommendation network, and commerce. This sends email, nothing else.
- README with a blunt warning: deliverability is DNS homework. Walk me through SPF,
  DKIM, and DMARC before the first send, budget an afternoon for it.
